messages:
Anna (Platform): Quick follow-up after the active/active RFC — we need a compact way to signal tenant geo-consent and desired residency to the edge proxy. Two options on the table: per-tenant residency flag in control plane (server-side) or a client-sent hint header. Thoughts?
Ryan (Arch): Prefer control-plane first: a tenant-level residency stamp keeps decision centralized and auditable. Edge can cache stamp per-tenant.
Mike C: +1 for control-plane, but we need a fallback when stamp is missing (signup flows, migrations). client header as fallback seems reasonable.
Sophia (Legal): For EU PII we can't rely on client headers alone — they’re not proof of consent. If we default to client-header-only we risk routing EU data out of region. Control-plane authoritative, client-hint only for optimization.
Anna (Platform): Agreed. Operationally I want the edge to do: 1) consult cached tenant stamp 2) if missing, call control-plane sync endpoint 3) allow header only if tenant is in "opt-in-accept-headers" list.
Ryan (Arch): That maps to a small state machine. Quick sketch:
```
if cached_stamp -> route by stamp
else if control_plane says residency=X -> cache and route
else if tenant.accepts_headers && req.header(X-Resident) -> tentative route with lower SLA
else -> route-local-first with telemetry tag
```
Mike C: Important: when we do "tentative route" we should mark requests with a header like `X-Route-Origin: tentative` so downstream can treat it as possible non-resident write. Also increment a metric to catch bad routing.
Anna (Platform): Good call. We'll add a metric and a fallback-policy label. Also want a short TTL for cached_stamp (default 5m) to allow fast updates during rollouts.
Sophia (Legal): TTL must be auditable. For EU-regulated tenants, TTL shouldn't permit cross-border writes for the TTL window. Either force control-plane enforced route for regs or set TTL to 0.
Ryan (Arch): We can make TTL configurable per-tenant. For regulated tenants default TTL=0. For normal tenants 5m. Also add an operator override for emergencies.
Mike C: How do we handle failover? If primary region is down and tenant is EU-regulated we must not failover to non-EU. So policy needs a hard constraint: allowed_regions list per-tenant.
Anna (Platform): Exactly — control-plane will store allowed_regions and the edge will only fail over within that set. For non-regulated tenants we have a soft policy allowing cross-region failover.
Sophia (Legal): We also need audit logs for each decision: which stamp used, whether header was accepted, and which region served the write. Retention per contract.
infra-bot: Runbook link: https://playbook.redwood.local/geo-routing (contains operator override steps, metrics dashboard queries).
Ryan (Arch): Implementation notes: keep edge logic tiny. Fetch stamp via JWT-auth'd endpoint, store in local LRU with per-tenant meta (allowed_regions, ttl, accept_headers). Expose fast path for warm tenants.
Anna (Platform): Action items: Ryan to PR the edge state-machine + config, Mike to add metrics and header conventions, Sophia to confirm retention windows and legal wording. I'll wire the control-plane schema.
Ryan (Arch): I'll open PR by EOD with unit tests for header acceptance rules.
Mike C: I'll add `X-Route-Origin` and `X-Resident-Decision` header naming to the internal header doc.
Sophia (Legal): I'll post the retention requirements in thread and flag any tenants that must have TTL=0.
Anna (Platform): Awesome — if no objections we'll implement this pattern in the next canary. :thumbsup:
